records.title: CFTC March 20, 2026 crypto collateral FAQs — direct review
records.note: Directly reviewed official 5-page FAQ. Q7: a DCO may accept crypto, including payment stablecoins, as initial margin if assets meet Regulation 39.13(g)(10) minimal credit, market and liquidity risk. Q8: DCO sets risk/stress haircuts and reviews at least monthly. Q9: FCM must file notice with MPD via WinJammer before relying on Letter 26-05. Q10: during each FCM's first three months from commencement, only payment stablecoins, BTC and ETH may be accepted; event reporting applies; weekly asset-type reports run for three months from the calendar month after notice. Q11: after the initial three months, an FCM may accept other crypto assets if it continues to meet conditions (1)-(3) of Letter 26-05. Q1 permits customer non-security crypto after haircuts to secure debit/deficit balances in futures, foreign futures and cleared swaps accounts. Q3-Q5 prohibit proprietary non-stablecoin crypto as residual interest, do not authorize investment of customer funds in stablecoins, and do not make crypto eligible collateral for uncleared swaps. FAQ expressly says it creates no binding rights/rules and is staff guidance, not Commission action.

records.title: Bitnomial Clearinghouse current accepted collateral, haircut and member list
records.note: Current official page identifies Bitnomial Clearinghouse LLC as CFTC-registered DCO and lists clearing members including Hidden Road Partners CIV US LLC, Marex, NinjaTrader, R.J. O'Brien, Wedbush and Bitnomial Clearing LLC. Accepted collateral: BTC 15% haircut/$100M limit; ETH 20%/$45M; XRP 40%/$15M. XRP product maintenance-margin entries are 17%; these are separate controls from the 40% collateral haircut. Page does not disclose actual XRP balances/utilization or define the $15M limit basis.

records.title: Bitnomial Clearinghouse margin methodology and default waterfall
records.note: Official methodology page dated July 17, 2025 says margins target 99% of expected price movement over a historical period and portfolio margin uses CME SPAN over one day. It lists a $5M clearinghouse guaranty-fund contribution, up to $1M non-defaulting member assessments and contract extinguishment in the default waterfall. This is generic methodology; it does not reveal XRP collateral utilization or asset-specific stress parameters.

Tracks six US spot funds plus BITW; GXRP holdings remain in totals but flows are excluded due an issuer-page capture gap, and XRPR has look-through limitations. Do not reconcile with CryptoKeyhole without a per-fund/date crosswalk.
